steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrrooooooww!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Aaaaaaaaaaaahhh!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrrooooooww!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Mrrowaaaaah... Now you've got me mrowing!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrrow! We're falling!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What are you talkin—Argh, the wind's too strong! My mask!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: We're falling!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm holding on as tight as I can! You won't fall!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Rathalos! The Rathalos is falling!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The mask is covering my eyes! I can't see anything!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Noir Corne! Noir Cornnnne! L-Look what the R-Ra-Rathalos is charging toward!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: T-Toward what?!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: We're about to crash!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hold on... Finally, my mask's back in place!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Ahh! We're going to crash!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Meow! My notes... My tail... All fine. Thank heavens!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Where are we? It's dark here...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Corne...! Noir Corne! Are you still alive?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrrow... I can only see half your body there. Noir Corne, don't die...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm okay... but could you stop tugging on my leg?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I have a lamp in my equipment bag. Turn it on.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Lamp? What's that? Mew mean this thing?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, now flip the switch at the bottom.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrow! That's bright! But it's not hot at all... How do you do it?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Another thing. My horn... It's stuck in this rock. Could you come help me out?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Your horn's... stuck in the rock...! Meowhahaha!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey! Don't laugh!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I'm on meow way.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Climb up from over there. Ahh! Don't climb me! And definitely don't grab that!

spans.text: Climb up from over there. Ahh! Don't climb

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Here I am... Is this where you're stuck? Wham!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Oww... My butt.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Where's the Rathalos? Did you see it?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: It went inside.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The opening of this cave's too high up. It'd take us too much work to climb up without help. We need to find a way to signal Yato, but we also can't lose track of the Rathalos...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Wait, where are we anyway?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I was going to ask mew!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The Rathalos went down the cave, and the cave only further down... Maybe it's connected to the one closer to the village. Looks like we'll have to head that way to check it out.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, Scholar! Wait up! What's the rush?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Meow! We need to hurry!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: There are so meowny mysteries! The laws of nature here aren't all that diffurent from where we're from, but there are all these situations I can't wrap my head around! The Rathalos is acting way too oddly!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Oddly? That new Felyne mentioned something about it being abnormal, too.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I'll explain to mew as we walk!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: The Rathalos burrowed itself down here... Purrhaps the cause of its odd behavior can be found here, too!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I swear this on the name of a furmer Royal Pawleontology Scriveners scholar! I will get to the bottom of this!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Noir Corne... come check this out.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm coming—Goodness, this stinks... Huh?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Scholar... Are these...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: All animal carcasses... all shredded and torn apart by the Rathalos.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Shellbeasts, hornbeasts, fowlbeasts... so many different beasts... Did it kill all these animals for food? Are these... leftovers?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: No, a Rathalos's bite can crush even bones. There is no way it would leave behind so many carcasses.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: They all look very complete, too. They were killed, but there are no chew marks or signs of them having been eaten...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Come. Let's check out what's up ahead.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrow! How could this be...?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What did you find?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: The carcasses here have all been burnt to a crisp... They were killed and dragged all the way down here, but it still spat fire at them. There's no way it could've eaten any of these.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Is it... angry?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Look here. This, this, and this! Not one of them... It didn't eat even a single one of them!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Purrhaps... the Rathalos can't eat Terran creatures?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Could that explain uh... how it's abnormal?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I don't know... Hunger can change its behavior, but it's hard to say for sure that's the reason...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Why? I don't get it at all!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Based on my observation data, Terran creatures follow the same growth patterns as where we're from. Besides, I ate the same food as you, and there's nothing wrong with me meow!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: This is just a guess, but... what if it's not caused by the food, but by the... Originium on its skin?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: You mean Rathalos caught Oripathy?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: —! Look at that!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: What mrow?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Quick! Help me get all these animals out of the way. The dirt, too.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: It stinks! Why can't you do it yourself?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Well, you tricked me into holding that fincatching rod for you. This is payback.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrow? *Hiss*... I'm mad! Mad, I tell you, mrow!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Wait, cut it out.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: ...I think I know why there are those traces of Originium on the Rathalos's body now.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Are you talking about the holes we're digging? What could they pawssibly imply?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: These are tracks left behind by Originium mining. The area underneath is most likely...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: An Originium mine.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: If this mine is why the villagers have been going so far to hide this cave from us, then that would explain everything.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Wait! What do you mean? Meow exactly does it explain anything?

spans.text: Wait! What do you mean? Meow exactly does it explain

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Considering Higashi's current situation and its dwindling resources... a private Originium mine that's hidden from the outside world could bring them piles of cash even if all they do is sell crude ore.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: But if any outsiders—maybe even greater forces—were to find out about their hidden mine, it could very well get taken over by force. It might even put their lives in danger.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: So what you're saying is, Originium is a kind of meowneral that's find in the earth, and the villagers have been digging it up?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: And you people do that on a regular basis?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: As I recall, you said Originium can cause an incurable disease called Oripathy, or even a cat-astrophic disaster that tears even the land and the sky apart...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: So why could you pawssibly want to dig it up?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Uh... because it's an energy source, I guess?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Energy source? You can burn wood and oil for heat, and you can boil water to purr-pel machines. Can't you people do any of that fur energy?

spans.text: Energy source? You can burn wood and oil for heat, and you can boil water to purr-pel machines. Can't you people do

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I can't think of a good reason fur willingly exposing yourselves to something so dangerous!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What did the Doctor say again... We Terrans use Originium through Originium Arts...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Thanks to advancements in Originium engine technology, Originium became widely used as an industrial energy source. And in the past, it was also often used for casting Arts...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I don't know any Arts, though. How I can explain this to you with something else...? Oh, hand me the light.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: What are mew doing with it? Mrowah! Don't take it apart! You'll purrt it out!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Here. This is what I'm talking about.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Huh? It's still lit up?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Take a look at this. This is a battery. It's what powers the light bulb up here, and that's how it's lit up.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: What does that have to do with Originium?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: The battery has Originium in it, too. There's also this... what do you call it... Arts Unit? That's the thing that turns the battery's Originium into electrical currents that light up the bulb.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: So it lights up beclawse of Originium?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Not only that, the light bulb, the outer shell, and all the parts inside were mass produced in a factory.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mass produced?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: It's when you make the same thing over and over on a large scale. Take this exploration lamp. A huge factory can make over a thousand of them in a day.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: A thousand?! That's so convenient! Could the clothes all the villagers wear pawssibly be made in those factories, too?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: That's right. The factory uses machines to build these parts, and what's driving those machines is called an Originium engine.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And they need Originium to function. That's how it is in most places here.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: So Terra's technology... and even its civilizations are built on a furndation of Originium.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I guess that's about it?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: But our Hunters don't have lamps, or the kind of clothes mew wear. The lamp is convenient, I'll give mew that...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: But even without something as dangerous as Originium, we get by just fine.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: It should be pawssible to replace it with something else here too, shouldn't it?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Are these Hunters common where you guys are from?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Of course. If we leave the meownsters be, they could pose significant threats to the villagers' safety, and our livelihoods depend on the meowterials you get out of them.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: So... are all the hunts these hunters go on safe?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: No... Most of the time, there are dangers everywhere. You're more likely to fail a hunt than succeed.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: And there's only a very small number of truly skilled hunters. When they are up against truly tricky monsters, meowst hunters end up losing their lives.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Then our Originium's actually not a whole lot different from your monsters.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrow? What do you mean?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Both Originium and monsters are unpreventable threats, but they both also give us the opportunity to survive.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrrow...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You probably won't see one, but... Catastrophes are actually very common here in Terra. Most folks live in the nomadic cities, and each city can have tens of thousands of residents.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: When a Catastrophe is about to strike, the entire city starts moving.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: A city with tens of thousands of residents... moving... That sounds moewvelous. How do you move something that big?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Originium. Only the energy hidden in Originium can move a nomadic city. No other energy source comes close.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I can't believe this, mrow...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: We all definitely understand that using Originium can cause Catastrophes.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: But... when Catastrophe strikes, if you want to survive, even if all you have nearby is a twig or branch floating in a puddle, you're bound to grab it.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: It doesn't matter if it has thorns... That's the least of your worries.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Before nomadic cities were invented, before we started using Originium at the scale we do now, many more people died from Catastrophes.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Terra... sounds so scary, mrow.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Those thorns may end up cutting your fingers, but a Catastrophe's not going to end just because of your pain. You have no choice but to hold on... and hold on for dear life.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And it doesn't matter how hard you look. Until you find a smooth tree branch that won't cut you, that's all you can do.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: It doesn't matter how difficult it all is. You just have to grit your teeth and live on...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Noir Corne, I can hardly call you smart just for this, but purrhaps you have a point...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Thinking about it now, the difficulties we face aren't all that diffurent.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: The materials we need to forge weapons that can take on the fiercest beasts likewise come from fierce beasts, and behind that must be a countless number of sacrifices too...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: There are Hunters who never return from their hunts, Commission members who fall while exploring the New World, and plenty of Scriveners who disappeared without a trace while observing dangerous creatures for data...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: *sigh*... looks like no matter where mew are, people are fragile, and the world is a cruel place.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: But even if all that suffering is inevitable, and you have to pay the price to survive, must innocent lives be sacrificed too?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I've never heard of things like that where I'm from... Things like Originium which makes the innocent suffer.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: They don't catch Oripathy because they wanted to, and they won't even get to live without treatment. How could that pawssibly be right?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Of course it's not right.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mrow! So quick to answer!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Which is why somebody has to step forward and take on the burden of showing everyone else the way forward.
Hello? Is anybody there?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: What's that noise?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Did someone just talk?
Stop chatting! Look over here!
I've been stuck in here for three days now. Could you come over and move the stuff blocking this door?!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: She's asking us for help... Where are you? We're coming right away!
Whoa, watch out! There's about to be another beast outbreak.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Beast outbreak?
You can more or less figure it out from the name, can't you? It's an outbreak of all the animals in the forest going berserk at once.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I think I hear a familiar noise, too.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I can hear it, too. It's not coming again, is it?
Whenever you see a surge of animals here, you can bet they're all Infected.
